subject: P0: Subaru Digital — westus2 egress/latency spike and emergency geo-failback

From: Alan Kim <alan.kim@subaradigital.com>

Cc: ops@subaradigital.com
Date: Tue, 19 Oct 2027 08:12:03 -0700
Subject: P0: Production latency & 5xx spike — westus2

Marissa / Vanessa —

We are seeing a sudden ~8x increase in median token latency and a sustained 5xx spike across our production traffic hitting westus2 starting ~07:50 PT. Throughput is down ~45% vs baseline; several customer-facing endpoints are timing out. The incidents dashboard shows egress failures and packet loss from the AZ.

Attached screenshot shows the error rate and a short trace sample. This is affecting our checkout flows and we are getting escalations from our ops team. Can Redwood confirm whether this is an infra-side routing/peering problem or something on our end? We need an immediate mitigation path and an expected time to restoration.

Please escalate to engineering leadership if needed — we require an exec bridge within 30 minutes if traffic isn't stable.

Alan
Alan Kim
Head of Platform Engineering, Subaru Digital
alan.kim@subaradigital.com

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 19 Oct 2027 08:26:51 -07:00
Subject: Re: P0: Production latency & 5xx spike — westus2

Marissa — quick tech note from initial triage (packet captures and host telemetry attached):

Findings (first 15 minutes):
- High loss observed on egress to provider ASN for westus2, consistent with ToR-level flaps in two racks servicing our serving clusters.
- KV-cache hit rate unchanged; errors originate during TLS handshake/connection establishment to the provider egress path.
- Model runner hosts are green otherwise; CPU/GPU utilization stable.

Recommendation (immediate):
1) Steer production traffic away from westus2 to eastus2 and centralus for the next 60–90 minutes (canary to 5% then 50% then full).
2) Bring up quantized model variants in eastus2 to reduce cold-start latency while nodes warm (we have warm pools in place — will reduce time-to-stable).
3) Keep read-only cache primed; avoid large parameter reloads.

Estimated impact: 60–90 minutes to reach >90% throughput restoration after canary. Potential small increase in tail latency for heavy sequences during warm-up.

I will start the steer now pending Marissa/Vanessa signoff to inform the customer and for Vanessa to request an exec bridge/credits if needed.

Attachments: netdiag-0826.txt, kvcache_state.log

—
Rishi Malhotra
Lead SRE — Serving Runtime, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 19 Oct 2027 08:35:17 -07:00
Subject: EXEC: Subaru Digital P0 — recommend 1-hr credit + bridge

Team —

Thanks for the quick triage. Rishi — please proceed with the traffic steering plan and keep the canary window tight. Hannah, coordinate the node warm-up and monitor tail latencies.

From the commercial side, Subaru will almost certainly ask for compensation and an executive update. I recommend we offer:
- Immediate exec bridge with Subaru (Jonas to join if available)
- A one-hour service credit (provisional) while we validate the incident scope — legal/finance to finalize
- A 2-hour postmortem session tomorrow with the Subaru platform team and our engineering leads

Suggested message to Alan (short):
"Alan — we’ve identified an egress disruption affecting westus2 and are steering traffic to eastus2 with an expected recovery window of ~60–90 minutes. We’ll join an exec bridge now and provide a full postmortem tomorrow. We’re also provisioning an interim one-hour service credit while we investigate."

Marissa — happy to send once you sign off.

—
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com

From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 19 Oct 2027 09:05:42 -07:00
Subject: Re: EXEC: Subaru Digital P0 — recommend 1-hr credit + bridge

Update — executed traffic steering at 08:40 PT (canary -> 20% -> 60% -> 100%) and warmed quantized runners in eastus2. Metrics attached. Observed:
- Throughput recovered to ~92% of baseline within 18 minutes of full steer.
- 5xx rate dropped from 7.3% -> 0.4% aggregate across affected endpoints.
- Median latency returned to within 10% of baseline; P95 elevated by ~15% during warm-up.

We have the bridge open now with Subaru ops and are prepared for postmortem tomorrow 10:00 PT. Recommend we:
- Confirm the 1-hour credit provisional until final scoping.
- Draft a postmortem that includes timeline, root cause (ToR flaps -> egress loss), and remediation steps (additional routing fallback & improved health detection thresholds).

Attachments: postfailover-metrics.csv, runbook_az_failback.pdf

—
Hannah Schmitt
Sr. Site Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.com

2) Please confirm the provisional 1-hour service credit and next steps for the postmortem.
